facts.why: Monty runs a protest campaign urging a vote for 'none of the above'. He does not ask anyone to vote for him, and he is forced to end the campaign when he starts leading as a write in.

Monty does buy a rare stamp (the Inverted Jenny gag) and posts a postcard to Granville and Baxter. The plot does not say what the postcard cost, so 'most expensive postcard ever sent' on the unprinted note is a stretch.

vibe.verdict: A neat ballpark scorecard that suits the exhibition game, but the main stunts of the film are missing and the badge gets the campaign wrong.
missing: None of the Above campaign (the mayor race)
The suite at the Plaza Hotel (Monty)
Warren Cox and the bribe (Granville and Baxter)
Angela Drake keeping the books (the law firm)
ideas: Swap the Vote Monty badge for 'None of the Above'
Add the Inverted Jenny postcard as a stamp on the sweets page, replacing 'Postage Stamps' plain note
Add a Plaza Hotel suite line to the bar side, replacing the 'Draft Beer' note
Swap the 'Roasted Peanuts' note for 'Thirty million in thirty days'
